- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79+ → 80+), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to correct.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing downward trends; delays in recognizing mean reversion.
- Tends to overreact to recent high values, creating artificial upward bias in later forecast days.
- Underestimates volatility in low-price zones (e.g., 70–75 range), leading to overly conservative forecasts.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fails to capture short-term volatility or sudden reversals.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled; forecasts remain too high even after price drops.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent high prices are not sufficiently weighted in forecasts.
